newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: Ahern to be elected Irish Prime Miniser on Thursday.
newsitem.headline: Ahern to be elected Irish Prime Miniser on Thursday.

text.p: Fianna Fail leader Bertie Ahern was set to become Prime Minister of a minority Irish government on Thursday after winning the backing of Independents for his plans to cut crime, taxes and to secure Northern Ireland peace.

Political sources said 45-year-old Ahern would be formally voted in as Taoiseach (Prime Minister) when parliament reconvened around 1500 (1400 GMT) for the first time since June 6 cliffhanger elections.

Ahern's Fianna Fail and its small electoral ally, the Progressive Democrats, have 81 of the 166 seats in parliament but are likely to be backed by a variety of independent legislators after weeks of behind-the-scenes talks.
He told Irish radio on Wednesday that he had reached "certain arrangements" with several Independents which are thought to include pledges to help develop rural areas.

Victory for Ahern's centre-right alliance ended almost three years of the centre-left coalition of John Bruton and returned seven Independents, two Green representatives and a member of Sinn Fein, political wing of IRA guerrillas.

Ahern has made clear that he would not seek the backing of Sinn Fein nor hold talks with its representative, Caoimhghin O' Caolain, until the Irish Republican Army ends its war against British rule of Northern Ireland.
Anglo-Irish plans to revive the Northern Ireland peace process are expected to be Ahern's first priority after he announces a cabinet on Thursday evening, the sources said.

Ray Burke, 53, was expected to be named Foreign Affairs minister with responsibility for Northern Ireland while the task of overseeing Ireland's entry into EMU was to be entrusted to Fianna Fail stalwart Charlie McCreevy, the sources said.

Confirmation of their appointments was not expected until Ahern was elected Prime Minister by parliament and had seen President Mary Robinson to complete the formalities of becoming Ireland's youngest premier on Thursday evening.
Burke is regarded by parliamentary colleagues as an astute politician and a "safe pair of hands" into which the Northern Ireland peace process can be entrusted.
The Anglo-Irish initiative received a boost on Wednesday when Britain formally offered Sinn Fein a seat at Belfast peace negotiations if the IRA calls a ceasefire.
McCreevy, 47, is seen as a tough-talking enemy of government spending who has already pledged to keep expenditure growth within four percent, half of which is for inflation.

He takes over an economy which is forging ahead and creating 1,000 jobs a week and will oversee the task of keeping the economy with the EU's Maastricht criteria so that Ireland can be among the first states to join EMU.

Economic and monetary union is the goal of all major Irish parties and Ahern is on record as saying that his government will not change its mind despite the persistent doubts of its biggest trading partner, Britain.
The formalities of forming a new government will be concluded on the first anniversary of the hit-man killing of Veronica Guerin, Ireland's most famous investigative reporter.

She is thought to have been ordered to be killed by a drugs baron she was investigating. One person has been charged with the crime and 186 questioned over an event which shocked the country and made it aware of the extent of organised crime.

A central pledge in Ahern's campaign was to introduce "zero-tolerance" methods of policing which would entail cracking down on every sort of minor crime to create a climate in which major offences would not be committed.
